SEAC continues to focus on several important areas, including concerns regarding discipline procedures and ensuring consistency in the manifestation determination review process. We are also examining equitable access to adapted physical

education and electives, continuing discussions around the development of the View Transition Center, and expansion of the Start on Success program, and exploring the impact of the new cut scores for the SOL assessments on students with disabilities. Our goal is to identify challenges, strengthen consistency, and advocate appropriate supports and opportunities for all students with disabilities. Next slide, please.

Our policy and compliance subcommittee continues to focus on concerns relating to the implementation of IDEA procedures, including the manifestation determination review process. Our priorities include identifying opportunities to strengthen consistency in how these procedures are implemented across LCPS schools, ensuring that students with disabilities receive the procedural protections they are entitled to, and developing recommendations that support students and families.

Ultimately, our goal is to promote consistent practices, strengthen accountability, and help ensure that the rights and educational needs of students with disabilities remain at the forefront of the decision-making process. Next slide, please. Our specialized reading and math subcommittee continues to focus on strengthening instructional practices, ensuring consistency in assessments, and improving access to appropriate accommodations and supports for students with disabilities.

One of our key priorities is examining the inconsistencies on how common assessments are administered across LCPS schools, improving communication with families, clarifying the accommodations, modifications, and interventions available to students. We are also placing particular emphasis on the writing instruction. This includes exploring VDOE-approved instructional programs, identifying individualized strategies for students with

writing difficulties, and examining evidence-based supports that extend beyond traditional graphic organizers and editing checklists. Additionally, the subcommittee is seeking greater clarity regarding the relationship between the MTSS support plans and student accommodations, including whether an MTSS plan is required for a read-aloud accommodation. The goal is to promote consistent practices, strengthen specialized

instruction, and ensure students with disabilities have equitable access to instructional supports and accommodations they need to succeed. Next slide, please. The Meaningful Inclusion Subcommittee continues to focus on ensuring that students with disabilities have equitable access to educational opportunities and meaningful participation in all aspects of school experience. One of our key priorities is

improving guidance around double rostering for students who participate in both special education programs and general education classes. We want to ensure that scheduling and enrollment practices support meaningful inclusion rather than create barriers to participation. We are also examining equitable K12 specials and electives, including art, music, physical education,

adapted physical education, library, and secondary elective courses. Additionally, the subcommittee is working to identify potential barriers related to staffing, facilities, equipment, and scheduling that may limit opportunities for students with disabilities to participate alongside their peers. As part of this work, we are gathering information and data to better understand these challenges and develop informed recommendations.

Next slide, please. The Transition Subcommittee continues to focus on strengthening transition services and ensuring students with disabilities are prepared for life beyond high school. One of our key priorities is promoting consistent life skills and community-based instruction beginning in middle school so students have opportunities to develop the independence, confidence, and practical skills needed for adulthood.

We are also focused on expanding inclusive vocational and work-based learning opportunities that allow students to explore career interests, gain meaningful employment experiences, and develop skills alongside their peers. Additionally, the subcommittee is supporting the development of the View Transition Academy and advocating for the expansion of the Start on Success program to provide students with additional

pathways towards employment and post-secondary success. Another important priority is improving family awareness of available transition services, resources, and post-secondary options while strengthening individualized, student-centered transition planning that reflects each student's strength, interest, and goals. SEAC's goal is to ensure that transition planning is not simply about preparing

students to graduate, but about preparing them for meaningful, fulfilling lives beyond the classroom with opportunities for continued education, employment, independence, and community participation. Next slide, please. SEAC recognizes the importance of our annual parent and guardian survey in understanding families' experiences, identifying areas of improvement, and recognizing concerns that

may require further attention. We believe these findings deserve a thoughtful and comprehensive review. Therefore, SEAC will continue to examine the survey results, including year-over trends, areas of continued need, and opportunities to inform the work of our subcommittees. We are currently in the process of securing the platform for a comprehensive analysis. We look forward to returning to the school board this spring to share a more detailed analysis of the findings,

as well as any potential recommendations. For tonight, we wanted to acknowledge the importance of this while keeping our primary focus on SEAC's budget recommendations. Next slide, please. SEAC prioritize focus on strengthening instructional support, protecting essential staffing, expanding specialized programs, and ensuring equitable access to services. As LCPS navigates

enrollment changes and budget challenges, we believe special education resources must remain aligned with students' needs, not simply enrollment numbers. SEAC recommends increasing our special education instructional facilitators. As LCPS continues to expand specialized programs, it is important that teachers, particularly those new to special

education or specialized programs, receive the support necessary to implement instruction effectively. SIFs play a critical role in providing instructional coaching, helping teachers implement specialized curricula, interventions, and promoting consistency across schools. Their expertise help ensure that programs are not only available, but are being implemented as intended.

SEAC is requesting that LCPS prioritize protecting special education teacher positions, particularly secondary cross-categorical teachers, to ensure staffing levels remain aligned with students' needs and services required by their IEPs. As LCPS experiences changes in enrollment, staffing decisions must continue to reflect the actual need of students receiving special education services.

A decline in overall student enrollment does not necessarily mean a decline in special education caseloads. It's quite the opposite. The number of students receiving special education services continue to climb despite overall enrollment numbers decreasing. The complexity of students' needs or the number of services required by their IEPs must be part of the conversation.

Secondary cross-categorical teachers are particularly important because they support students with a wide range of disabilities, instructional needs across multiple academic settings. SEAC has identified a need to expand as what we are referring to as the tweener supports. These are students who remain on the general education curriculum and SOL track, but require more intensive academic interventions,

instructional adaptations, smaller learning environments, or social-emotional support than a traditional classroom setting may provide. These students often fall between existing program models, creating challenges for students trying to provide appropriate levels of support. LCPS has begun piloting approaches at the elementary level to address these needs, but the availability of these supports remain

inconsistent across schools. SEAC encourages expanding these opportunities, particularly at the elementary level, while also evaluating the need for additional support at the middle school level. Our goal is to ensure students have access to appropriate interventions and learning environments while maintaining opportunities to participate in the general education setting. We are recommending prioritizing CAST transportation needs.

Students participating in CAST programs require transportation that is safe, reliable, and accessible. Concerns have been raised regarding aging vehicles and the need for transportation options that appropriately accommodate students with disabilities, including those with mobility needs. Reliable transportation is essential to ensuring students can consistently access

educational programming, community-based instruction, and other learning opportunities associated with these programs. SEAC encourages LCPS to evaluate the condition and accessibility of the existing vehicles and prioritize necessary replacements or improvements. SEAC encourages LCPS to provide adequate adapted physical education staffing and dedicated scheduling capacity.

APE is an important part of ensuring students with disabilities have meaningful access to physical education that meets their individual needs and abilities. Providing these services require appropriate staffing, specialized instruction, scheduling that allows students to participate consistently. Without sufficient staffing and dedicated scheduling opportunities, schools face many challenges delivering these services effectively.

SEAC recommends ensuring adapted PE and all specials are appropriately supported so students can access the physical education opportunities and services they require. SEAC is advocating for the development of an additional public separate programming option within LCPS. SEAC has consistently emphasized the importance of maintaining a full continuum of special education services and placement options.

Currently, there are students whose needs may not be appropriately met within their existing school setting, but for whom private day placement may not be the most appropriate alternative. This creates a gap in the continuum of services available to families and IEP teams. Developing an additional LCPS public separate option could provide more specialized educational environment while

allowing students to remain within public school divisions when appropriate. SEAC is recommending strengthening and appropriately compensating our special education dean positions. Special education deans carry significant responsibilities related to special education programming, compliance, staff support, and coordination of services at the school level. These responsibilities require specialized knowledge, experience,

and leadership to help ensure students receive appropriate services and that schools meet their special education obligations. SEAC encourages LCPS to review current stipend structure and consider whether compensation appropriately reflects the scope and complexity of the responsibilities. We are also recommending to clarify the role, the qualification, and the reporting structure for these positions to promote

consistency and effective special education leadership across schools. Next slide, please. Beyond these immediate budget priorities, SEAC is raising an important long-term concern regarding the declining enrollment and potential future budget reductions. As LCPS plans for the future enrollment changes, we believe special education staffing and services should

not automatically be reduced by the same percentage as overall student enrollment. A reduction in enrollment does not necessarily mean a corresponding reduction in the number of students requiring special education services, the complexity of their needs, or the staffing necessary to fulfill their IEP requirements. For that reason, SEAC is advocating for LCPS to establish a protected

core of special education staffing and direct student services. This means identifying the essential staffing and services necessary to meet students' needs and ensuring resources receive appropriate protections when future budget reductions are considered. We also recommend that LCPS develop a comprehensive special education budget framework, including a special education impact analysis before significant reductions

are adopted. This analysis should consider how proposed reductions could affect staffing levels, caseloads, specialized programs, related services, transition supports, assistive technology, and LCPS's ability to meet its special education obligation. Our goal is to begin the conversation now before significant reductions are proposed, so that decisions affecting students with disabilities are made thoughtfully,

transparently, and with a clear understanding of their potential impact. Ultimately, SEAC recommendations reflect a shared goal, ensuring that students with disabilities have access to appropriate staff, programs, services, and learning environments they need to succeed. As LCPS navigates changes in enrollment and future budget challenges, we ask the school board to

recognize special education needs cannot be measured by enrollment numbers alone. Our hope is that these recommendations will not only address current gaps in services but also help ensure a more sustainable and consistent approach to special education planning. We appreciate the board's consideration for these priorities and its continued commitment to meet the needs of students with disabilities throughout LCPS. Next slide, please.
